title: Qualcomm and Arm kick off trial, potential for huge damages in focus
source_used: Reuters (wire text read in The Economic Times' copy)
key_facts: Qualcomm and Arm Holdings were due in court on Monday 5 Oct 2026 for a five-day jury trial in US federal court in Delaware.

Qualcomm accuses Arm of withholding chip testing tools that were due under contract, and alleges Arm leaked to the media its 2024 threat to terminate a vital license agreement, damaging talks for a chip deal between Qualcomm and Meta Platforms.
Qualcomm, one of Arm's largest customers, is seeking to quit paying royalties, potentially worth billions of dollars, to Arm for up to five years.
Judge Maryellen Noreika is weighing whether to throw out that term of the contract, which could mean Qualcomm could seek only a smaller amount of damages.

Arm, owned by Japan's SoftBank Group, denies breaching the contract and calls the damage to Qualcomm's chip deals speculative; it also argues Qualcomm cannot seek damages for the leak because Qualcomm leaked non-public details of antitrust probes into Arm.
Arm sued Qualcomm in 2022 alleging contract breaches; Qualcomm won a key victory in 2024.

In a related bench trial (judge only) the same judge will hear whether Arm negotiated in good faith with Qualcomm over the next version of Arm's chip technology; Qualcomm's agreement with Arm runs through 2033.

Qualcomm is a major maker of chips for Android phones and has expanded into data-centre chips; Arm has for decades supplied core chip-design technology to Qualcomm and others such as Nvidia, and has become a competitor to those customers by releasing chips of its own.
quote_evidence: Chipmaker Qualcomm and chip tech firm Arm Holdings, long at loggerheads, will once again be in court on Monday with Qualcomm accusing Arm of withholding chip testing tools that were due under contract.
The five-day jury trial will mark yet another stage in the contentious relationship between the two firms.
Qualcomm’s agreement with Arm runs through 2033.
why_it_matters_hint: The trial could decide whether Qualcomm, one of Arm's largest customers, can stop paying royalties potentially worth billions of dollars.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 (trial opening, federal court in Delaware)
